name: The Silence-Bells
summary: Forty-one bronze bells lining the Veiled Gate at Ashveil Cross, cast from melted Concord coin by the town's founders. They hang motionless in wind and storm alike — until the Quiet stirs, when they swing without sound. Warden Kell's private tally of silent-rings is the continent's best data on the scar's growth, and the bells have never once rung aloud. Nobody knows what would happen if they did.
origin: ~50–100 AA, when the King's Road crossing was chartered; bronze from Concord coin hoards
current_whereabouts: Along the mile of paved road through the Quiet's edge, Ashveil Cross.
properties: Swing without sound when the Quiet moves — the only instrument that consistently detects its advance
Deaf to everything else: storms, caravans, shouting children leave them still
Local custom forbids ringing any bell within a mile of the Gate 'in case it teaches them'
keepers: Warden Kell maintains them; the stone-wardens re-hang each bell yearly; nobody has ever tolled one deliberately.
value_or_danger: To the Crown and Censer: priceless data. To whoever makes one ring: unknown, which is the danger.
adventure_hooks: All forty-one rang last night — silently, together, for an hour. Kell needs witnesses who will say so publicly.
Players are asked to retrieve a bell stolen from the Vitrified Square in Karvess: rung once, it might answer the towers.
A bell-founder claims he can recast a cracked bell using Quiet-side bronze; the Censer wants him stopped, the barons want him funded.

rarity.note: Forty-one bells tuned by proximity to the Quiet itself.
